y-m-06-05.title: Wetin be di smallest number of students di winner fit get?
y-m-06-05.topic: Reading data: relationship between most chosen thing and total number of people
y-m-06-05.goal: Test statement "winner na at least half of total" by making counterexamples, and work out how many students winner gatz get at minimum so only one winner dey.
y-m-06-05.material:
20 students each choose one school lunch menu from tteokbokki, gimbap, ramyeon, and dumplings. Each person choose only one. If only one menu get most choices, we call dat menu di "winner". If two or more menus tie for most, we talk say no winner dey.
Jaei talk, "Di winning menu must be chosen by at least 10 students. Na half of 20."
y-m-06-05.thinking.1: Making several tables wey follow conditions
y-m-06-05.thinking.2: Finding smallest case and stating di limit
y-m-06-05.prereq.0: Splitting numbers up to 20 into several parts
y-m-06-05.s.s1.prompt: Wetin good way to find out whether Jaei statement always correct?
y-m-06-05.s.s1.hint.0: Write in words how table wey be exact opposite of Jaei statement go look.
y-m-06-05.s.s1.hint.1: Choose one number of votes for winner wey good to test first.
y-m-06-05.s.s1.o.a: Make one more table where winner get 10 students.
y-m-06-05.s.s1.r.a: Case with 10 already fit di statement. To find whether table wey go against statement dey, you need look for another case.
y-m-06-05.s.s1.o.b: Make table where all four menus get same number.
y-m-06-05.s.s1.r.b: If dem all same, no winner dey, so you no fit test di statement.
y-m-06-05.s.s1.o.c: Assume Jaei correct and look for reason.
y-m-06-05.s.s1.r.c: If you start from idea say e correct and only look for reasons, you fit miss cases where statement break.
y-m-06-05.s.s1.o.d: Make table where winner get fewer than 10 students.
y-m-06-05.s.s1.r.d: Dis thinking try make example wey go against statement by yourself.
y-m-06-05.s.s1.explain: Word "must" break if you fit make even one table wey go against am. Try find table where only one winner dey and e get fewer than 10 students.
y-m-06-05.s.s2.prompt: Make two different tables wey show Jaei statement wrong. Tteokbokki must win (get more than every other menu), tteokbokki get 9 students or fewer, and four menus altogether get 20 students.
y-m-06-05.s.s2.hint.0: Choose tteokbokki number and split remaining students among di other three menus.
y-m-06-05.s.s2.hint.1: Check one by one whether all three menus get fewer than tteokbokki.
y-m-06-05.s.s2.ok.c1: Student numbers na natural numbers 0 or more.
y-m-06-05.s.s2.fail.c1: Student numbers must be natural numbers wey be 0 or more.
y-m-06-05.s.s2.fail.c2: Four menus must add up to 20 students.
y-m-06-05.s.s2.ok.c3: Tteokbokki get more than every other menu, so na di winner.
y-m-06-05.s.s2.fail.c3: Tteokbokki must get more than each of gimbap, ramyeon, and dumplings.
y-m-06-05.s.s2.ok.c4: Winner get 9 students or fewer, so e go against wetin Jaei talk.
y-m-06-05.s.s2.fail.c4: If winner get 10 students or more, e fit Jaei statement. Try 9 students or fewer.
y-m-06-05.s.s2.explain: For example, tteokbokki 6, gimbap 5, ramyeon 5, dumplings 4 add up to 20 students, and tteokbokki win but get fewer than 10. So statement "winner must get at least 10" wrong. Tables wey gimbap, ramyeon, and dumplings swap places count as same case.
y-m-06-05.s.s3.prompt: When 20 students each choose one of four menus, and only one winner dey, wetin be smallest number of students wey fit choose di winning menu?
y-m-06-05.s.s3.hint.0: Set winner at 5 students, and write di most di other three menus fit get altogether if each one get fewer than 5.
y-m-06-05.s.s3.hint.1: Compare dat highest number with 20 students.
y-m-06-05.s.s3.r.a: If you split 20 students equally among four menus, each get 5. But if dem all get same number, no single winner dey.
y-m-06-05.s.s3.r.b: If winner get 5, all di rest get 4 or fewer, so e no reach enough. E become possible from 6 students.
y-m-06-05.s.s3.r.c: Na true say table with 7 dey, but check whether smaller number fit too.
y-m-06-05.s.s3.r.d: 10 students na number Jaei talk. We just make table with fewer.
y-m-06-05.s.s3.explain: If winner get 5, other three menus each get 4 or fewer, so 5+4+4+4=17 no reach 20. With 6, you fit make 6+5+5+4=20. So winner get at least 6.

y-m-06-02.title: Our thinking dey change each time survey results arrive?
y-m-06-02.topic: Collecting data: statements wey change with number of people surveyed
y-m-06-02.goal: Compare result from asking some people with result from more people, realize say how much you fit trust am dey change, and find cases wey person wey never answer fit change result.
y-m-06-02.material: Grade 2 Class 3 get 24 students altogether. Dem wan choose picnic snack from jelly, cookies, and bread, and each person go choose only one. Survey results dey come little by little. As you read results wey arrive, change your thinking about wetin go be good choice, or leave am as e be.
y-m-06-02.thinking.0: Correcting your judgment or leaving am as e be, depending on new data
y-m-06-02.thinking.1: Being careful not to stretch result from some people to whole group
y-m-06-02.thinking.2: Finding conditions wey go make result change
y-m-06-02.prereq.1: Reading number of students from table
y-m-06-02.s.s1.prompt: Read data in order as e arrive, and each time choose judgment wey you fit make now.
y-m-06-02.s.s1.hint.0: Compare whether result wey arrive dis time support or go against earlier judgment.
y-m-06-02.s.s1.hint.1: Count whether people wey never answer still dey.
y-m-06-02.s.s1.st.0.info: First, dem ask 6 students. 4 choose jelly, 1 choose cookies, and 1 choose bread. 18 students never answer yet.
y-m-06-02.s.s1.st.0.ask: With dis result, wetin we suppose do about snack for class of 24?
y-m-06-02.s.s1.st.0.after: Jelly dey ahead, but 18 students still remain, so e too early to settle am as whole-class result. Guessing and asking more people both okay.
y-m-06-02.s.s1.st.0.o.a: Most people choose jelly, so jelly go be di most for whole class too.
y-m-06-02.s.s1.st.0.r.a: Dis one carry result of 6 students straight go whole class. We still no know how di other 18 go choose.
y-m-06-02.s.s1.st.0.o.b: Dem ask only 6 students, so e too early to choose snack for whole class.
y-m-06-02.s.s1.st.0.r.b: Dis notice say plenty people still dey wey we no know about.
y-m-06-02.s.s1.st.0.o.c: Jelly seem to dey ahead, so make guess for now and ask more people.
y-m-06-02.s.s1.st.0.r.c: Dis thinking use current result as basis for guess without settling am, and try to find out more.
y-m-06-02.s.s1.st.0.o.d: Cookies and bread get only 1 each, so remove dem as choice from start.
y-m-06-02.s.s1.st.0.r.d: Dis cross out small numbers as choices, even though we still no know wetin di other people go choose.
y-m-06-02.s.s1.st.1.info: Now dem don ask all 20 students wey dey present (including first 6). 7 choose jelly, 9 choose cookies, and 4 choose bread.
y-m-06-02.s.s1.st.1.ask: Choose wetin you fit talk from dis result.
y-m-06-02.s.s1.st.1.after: Di result from first 6 students become less strong compared with di 20. Among di 20, you fit talk say cookies most and bread fewest. To talk about all 24, e still no enough.
y-m-06-02.s.s1.st.1.o.a: Among di 20 students dem ask, most people choose cookies.
y-m-06-02.s.s1.st.1.r.a: Dis statement read di result for 20 as e be.
y-m-06-02.s.s1.st.1.o.b: Jelly plenty among first 6, so jelly na di most.
y-m-06-02.s.s1.st.1.r.b: Dis still trust result from first 6. Compare am with result for 20 wey just come.
y-m-06-02.s.s1.st.1.r.c: Dis statement compare di three numbers and read dem.
y-m-06-02.s.s1.st.1.o.d: 9 choose cookies, so decide say cookies go be di most for class of 24 too.
y-m-06-02.s.s1.st.1.r.d: Dis stretch result for 20 straight go result for all 24. Some people never come yet.
y-m-06-02.s.s1.st.2.info: But these 20 na friends wey dey present. Di 4 wey absent dat day never choose. Result for 20 of 24 be as above.
y-m-06-02.s.s1.st.2.ask: Wetin we suppose do to choose snack?
y-m-06-02.s.s1.st.2.after: Di 4 absent students fit change result. For next step, find by yourself how much dem fit change am. Thought 'choose cookies but talk say e fit change' okay, and thought 'ask di 4 first' okay too.
y-m-06-02.s.s1.st.2.o.a: Di result fit change depending on how di 4 absent students choose, so ask di 4 too.
y-m-06-02.s.s1.st.2.r.a: Dis thinking consider whether di remaining people fit change result.
y-m-06-02.s.s1.st.2.o.b: Cookies na the most now, so choose cookies, but talk say e fit change depending on result from di 4 absent students.
y-m-06-02.s.s1.st.2.r.b: Dis use current result and also state condition say decision no settle yet.
y-m-06-02.s.s1.st.2.o.c: Choose cookies, assuming say di 4 absent students all choose cookies too.
y-m-06-02.s.s1.st.2.r.c: We no know how absent friends go choose, but dis assume say dem go choose like current result.
y-m-06-02.s.s1.st.2.o.d: We no fit trust result for 20, so start di survey again from beginning.
y-m-06-02.s.s1.st.2.r.d: Dis throw away all results wey dem collect already. Check whether e enough to ask only di 4 we no know about.
y-m-06-02.s.s1.reflect: Result of first 6, result of 20 present, and fact about 4 wey never answer each change 'how much we fit say'. You no gatz stick with judgment once you make am, and e good to say am with condition wey fit current result.
y-m-06-02.s.s2.prompt: Say each of di 4 absent students choose only jelly or cookies (nobody choose bread). If k of dem choose jelly, then (4-k) choose cookies. When you add these 4 students choices to result for 20 (jelly 7, cookies 9, bread 4), find two different k values wey make jelly equal to or bigger than cookies, then enter dem.
y-m-06-02.s.s2.hint.0: Choose one value of k, and write on two lines how many students choose jelly and cookies each go be.
y-m-06-02.s.s2.hint.1: Change k one by one from 0 to 4 and compare di two numbers.
y-m-06-02.s.s2.var.k: Number of di 4 absent students wey choose jelly
y-m-06-02.s.s2.ok.c1: Whole-number count of people from 0 to 4.
y-m-06-02.s.s2.fail.c1: 4 absent students dey, so k must be one of 0, 1, 2, 3, 4.
y-m-06-02.s.s2.ok.c2: Jelly become equal to or bigger than cookies.
y-m-06-02.s.s2.fail.c2: For dis case, jelly smaller than cookies. Add k to 7 for jelly and (4-k) to 9 for cookies, then compare.
y-m-06-02.s.s2.explain: If k na 3, jelly na 10 and cookies na 10, so dem equal; if k na 4, jelly na 11 and cookies na 9. If k na 2 or less, cookies still ahead. So if 3 or more out of di 4 absent students choose jelly, result go change.

y-m-06-03.title: Three pictures really mean 3 people?
y-m-06-03.topic: Picture graph: why you need to know how many students one picture represent
y-m-06-03.goal: Realize say to talk number of people from picture graph, you need know number wey one picture represent. After you get dat information, decide values for picture graph wey fit conditions.
y-m-06-03.material:
Dem show number of students wey come library each day with picture graph. But line under graph wey say "one ◯ represent how many students" don erase. Half picture ◐ represent half of ◯. Dem never draw Wednesday and Thursday yet.
Monday: ◯ ◯ ◯
Tuesday: ◯ ◯ ◐
Jeongwu count pictures and talk, "Monday na 3 students."
y-m-06-03.thinking.0: Finding more information wey need before talking number
y-m-06-03.thinking.1: Making several values wey fit conditions after information dey available
y-m-06-03.thinking.2: Talking how to check a friend's statement
y-m-06-03.prereq.0: Counting number of pictures in picture graph
y-m-06-03.s.s1.prompt: To talk how many students come Monday, wetin first you need to know?
y-m-06-03.s.s1.hint.0: Write separately wetin you fit see and wetin you no fit see for Monday row.
y-m-06-03.s.s1.hint.1: Think about agreement wey need so 3 pictures go mean 3 students.
y-m-06-03.s.s1.o.a: How many students one picture represent
y-m-06-03.s.s1.r.a: You find agreement wey connect number of pictures with number of students.
y-m-06-03.s.s1.o.b: Which grade students wey come Monday dey
y-m-06-03.s.s1.r.b: Even if you know grade, you no fit tell how many students one picture represent.
y-m-06-03.s.s1.o.c: How many students wey come Monday borrow book
y-m-06-03.s.s1.r.c: Students wey borrow books and students wey come different. Wetin we wan know now na number of students wey come.
y-m-06-03.s.s1.o.d: Whether dem put pictures sideways or up and down
y-m-06-03.s.s1.r.d: Di direction wey dem put dem no change number.
y-m-06-03.s.s1.explain: We know number of pictures, but whether one picture mean 1, 2, or 5 students, na only graph explanation fit tell. Dem erase dat agreement, so we no fit decide number of students yet.
y-m-06-03.s.s2.prompt: We find out say one ◯ represent 2 students and one ◐ represent 1 student (Monday 6 students, Tuesday 5 students). From Monday to Thursday, 20 students come altogether. Make two different ways to choose numbers of students wey come Wednesday and Thursday, wey dem never draw yet. Wednesday must get more than Thursday, and Thursday must get at least 1 student.
y-m-06-03.s.s2.hint.0: First write number of students for Monday and Tuesday, then think how many students remain.
y-m-06-03.s.s2.hint.1: Choose one number for Wednesday and match Thursday to am, then check say Wednesday bigger.
y-m-06-03.s.s2.var.w: Number of students wey come Wednesday
y-m-06-03.s.s2.var.t: Number of students wey come Thursday
y-m-06-03.s.s2.ok.c1: Student numbers na natural numbers, and Thursday too get at least 1 student.
y-m-06-03.s.s2.fail.c1: Student numbers must be natural numbers, and Thursday must get at least 1 student too.
y-m-06-03.s.s2.ok.c2: Di four days add up to 20 students.
y-m-06-03.s.s2.fail.c2: Monday 6 students and Tuesday 5 students, together with Wednesday and Thursday, must make 20 students.
y-m-06-03.s.s2.fail.c3: Wednesday must get more than Thursday.
y-m-06-03.s.s2.explain: Wednesday + Thursday na 9 students and Wednesday bigger, so (8,1), (7,2), (6,3), and (5,4) possible. You fit draw odd number using one ◐. For example, 7 students na 3 ◯ and 1 ◐.
y-m-06-03.s.s3.prompt: Tell Jeongwu how e fit check di statement "3 pictures mean 3 students." Write why you talk so too.
y-m-06-03.s.s3.hint.0: Write student number when 3 pictures dey, for case where one picture mean 1 student and case where e mean 2 students.
y-m-06-03.s.s3.hint.1: Compare whether student numbers for both cases na the same.
y-m-06-03.s.s3.selfAssess.0: Your writing include "how many students one picture stand for"?
y-m-06-03.s.s3.selfAssess.1: You write knowing say wetin Jeongwu talk fit be right or fit no be?
y-m-06-03.s.s3.selfAssess.2: One way dey wey Jeongwu fit follow to check am?
y-m-06-03.s.s3.model.0: You no fit talk straight away say 3 pictures mean 3 students. First you need know how many students one picture stand for. Look for explanation under graph.
y-m-06-03.s.s3.model.1: We no fit tell yet whether Jeongwu correct. One ◯ fit be 2 students or 5 students, so make we check how many students one picture represent.

y-m-06-01.title: We fit trust di result of sorting buttons?
y-m-06-01.topic: Sorting: choosing rule and checking result
y-m-06-01.goal: Choose sorting rules wey give same result no matter who sort, find place in sorted result wey no fit di rule and correct am, then sort by another rule by yourself.
y-m-06-01.material:
Harin wan sort 8 buttons into two groups. Color, shape, and number of holes for each button dey inside table below.
Button 1: red / circle / 2 holes
Button 2: blue / circle / 4 holes
Button 3: red / square / 4 holes
Button 4: yellow / circle / 2 holes
Button 5: blue / square / 2 holes
Button 6: yellow / square / 4 holes
Button 7: red / circle / 4 holes
Button 8: blue / circle / 2 holes
Harin sort according to number of holes and write di result. Check whether dem fit trust di result, and sort with another rule too.
y-m-06-01.thinking.1: Finding mistakes for sorted result and wrong way of checking
y-m-06-01.thinking.2: Sorting by another rule by yourself
y-m-06-01.prereq.0: Having sorted things by color, shape, and number
y-m-06-01.prereq.1: How to read each cell for table
y-m-06-01.s.s1.prompt: Choose all rules wey go give same result no matter who dey sort. (You fit only use wetin table write.)
y-m-06-01.s.s1.hint.0: For each rule, imagine whether two friends wey sort separately go get same result.
y-m-06-01.s.s1.hint.1: Check one by one whether wetin each rule use dey written for table.
y-m-06-01.s.s1.o.a: Whether e get 2 holes or 4 holes
y-m-06-01.s.s1.r.a: If you read number of holes for table, anybody go put button for same group. You notice say di rule clear.
y-m-06-01.s.s1.o.b: Whether na fine button or not
y-m-06-01.s.s1.r.b: Wetin look fine different for each person, so same button fit enter different groups.
y-m-06-01.s.s1.o.c: Whether na big or small button
y-m-06-01.s.s1.r.c: Table no show size, and e no settle how big go count as big. Different people fit sort differently.
y-m-06-01.s.s1.o.d: Whether na Harin favorite color or not
y-m-06-01.s.s1.r.d: Person wey no know Harin feeling no fit sort. Table alone no settle am.
y-m-06-01.s.s1.o.e: Whether shape na circle or square
y-m-06-01.s.s1.r.e: If you read shape column for table, anybody go get same result. You notice one more clear rule.
y-m-06-01.s.s1.explain: Dem fit read number of holes and shape wey table write, so anybody fit put button in same group. Whether e pretty, big, or somebody like am dey change by person or situation, or e no dey table, so we no fit talk say everybody get same result.
y-m-06-01.s.s2.prompt: Choose one line for Harin written result wey hard to believe. Several lines fit dey; you fit choose any one.
y-m-06-01.s.s2.hint.0: Find each button wey dem write inside groups from table one by one and check number of holes.
y-m-06-01.s.s2.hint.1: Separate whether each line copy wetin dem read from table or come from wetin dem read, then check evidence for each line.
y-m-06-01.s.s2.line.0: Rule: Sort buttons into ones with 2 holes and ones with 4 holes.
y-m-06-01.s.s2.line.3: 5 and 3 together make 8, and 8 buttons dey altogether, so result correct.
y-m-06-01.s.s2.explain: Line 2 get button 7, but for table button 7 get 4 holes. So line wrong. Line 3 write only 3 buttons with 4 holes, so dem leave 7 out, and dat result wrong too. Line 4 talk 'count na 8, so result correct too', but even if count correct, dem fit put buttons inside wrong groups. Correct result be: 2 holes: buttons 1, 4, 5, and 8; 4 holes: buttons 2, 3, 6, and 7. Line 1 correct.
y-m-06-01.s.s3.prompt: Sort 8 buttons into two groups using rule apart from number of holes. Write di rule and button numbers for each group, and write why everybody go get same result.
y-m-06-01.s.s3.hint.0: Choose either color or shape column for table and make two groups with yes-or-no question, like 'na red or not'.
y-m-06-01.s.s3.hint.1: After you write all di numbers for both groups, count whether all 8 dey included.
y-m-06-01.s.s3.placeholder: Example: Di rule na ... Di ... group na Buttons ..., ...
y-m-06-01.s.s3.selfAssess.0: Another person fit sort buttons by reading only my rule?
y-m-06-01.s.s3.selfAssess.1: You check each button number wey you write against table?
y-m-06-01.s.s3.selfAssess.2: Any button missing or dey inside both groups?
y-m-06-01.s.s3.model.0: I sort by color. Red group na Buttons 1, 3, 7 and non-red group na Buttons 2, 4, 5, 6, 8. You fit see color straight away, so everybody go get same result.
y-m-06-01.s.s3.model.1: I sort by shape. Circles na Buttons 1, 2, 4, 7, 8 and squares na Buttons 3, 5, 6. Everybody see whether na circle or square the same way.
y-m-06-01.s.s3.modelNote.1: Sorting into three groups, blue, yellow, and red, na one fine different way too.

y-m-06-04.title: Finding odd place inside voting result table
y-m-06-04.topic: Collecting data: comparing tally marks with total people
y-m-06-04.goal: Find wrong place for one count made with bundles and single marks, and explain say comparing total tally marks in result with number of people wey vote na one way to check am.
y-m-06-04.material:
Grade 2 Class 4 get 29 students altogether. During break, each person raise hand only once to choose game. Teacher make one mark at a time on board, and when 5 marks gather, tie dem into one bundle.
Tag: 1 bundle and 2 single marks
Jump rope: 1 bundle and 4 single marks
Dodgeball: 2 bundles and 3 single marks
Ara read marks and write result. Look wetin Ara write.
y-m-06-04.thinking.0: Checking reason for each line of solution
y-m-06-04.thinking.1: Checking whether result fit overall condition
y-m-06-04.prereq.0: How to read marks tied in groups of 5
y-m-06-04.prereq.1: Comparing size of numbers up to 30
y-m-06-04.s.s1.prompt: Choose di first wrong line for wetin Ara write.
y-m-06-04.s.s1.hint.0: For each line, check again how many votes one bundle represent.
y-m-06-04.s.s1.hint.1: For each line, calculate votes directly again from number of bundles and single tallies, and compare with calculation Ara write.
y-m-06-04.s.s1.line.0: Tag: 1 bundle and 2 single marks, so 5+2=7 votes
y-m-06-04.s.s1.line.1: Jump rope: 1 bundle and 4 single marks, so 5+4=9 votes
y-m-06-04.s.s1.line.2: Dodgeball: 2 bundles and 3 single marks, so 5+3=8 votes
y-m-06-04.s.s1.line.4: Class get 29 students but only 24 votes, so 5 students no vote.
y-m-06-04.s.s1.explain: E first go wrong for line 3. If 2 bundles dey, na 10 votes, but she count only 5. Dodgeball na 10+3=13 votes. Statement '5 students no vote' for line 5 na conclusion without support wey come from mistake for line 3. When dem correct and add dem up, 7+9+13=29 votes, wey equal number of students for class. Calculations for lines 1 and 2 and addition for line 4 correct.
y-m-06-04.s.s2.prompt: Ara total of 24 no match class 29 students. Wetin best make dem do first?
y-m-06-04.s.s2.hint.0: Think two or three things wey fit cause di difference between 24 and 29, and write dem down.
y-m-06-04.s.s2.hint.1: To check whether each reason wey you write correct, think wetin you suppose look at for blackboard or table.
y-m-06-04.s.s2.o.a: Find di 5 students wey no vote and make dem vote again.
y-m-06-04.s.s2.r.a: Dis blame people before considering other reasons. E never check whether counted result correct.
y-m-06-04.s.s2.o.b: Add 5 votes to Tag to make 29 votes.
y-m-06-04.s.s2.r.b: Dis make up votes to match di number. E match numbers, no be real votes.
y-m-06-04.s.s2.o.c: Count bundles and single marks for board again, line by line.
y-m-06-04.s.s2.r.c: Dis thinking try check counted result again.
y-m-06-04.s.s2.o.d: E no matter if total different, so leave am as e be.
y-m-06-04.s.s2.r.d: Dis notice di difference and ignore am. E clash with condition say each person vote only once.
y-m-06-04.s.s2.explain: Each person vote only once, so total number of all votes must be 29. If e no match, e good to first check counted result again.
y-m-06-04.s.s3.prompt: When each person vote only once, why e useful to compare total votes with number of students for class? Write one or two sentences.
y-m-06-04.s.s3.hint.0: Imagine wetin go happen to total votes if one person fit raise hand two times.
y-m-06-04.s.s3.hint.1: Write in words at least one reason why 29 and 24 different.
y-m-06-04.s.s3.placeholder: Example: Each person vote once, so ...
y-m-06-04.s.s3.selfAssess.0: Your writing include condition "each person vote once"?
y-m-06-04.s.s3.selfAssess.1: You talk wetin happen if total votes different from number of students for class?
y-m-06-04.s.s3.model.0: Each person vote only once, so adding all votes suppose equal di 29 students for class. If e different, dem count something wrong somewhere.
y-m-06-04.s.s3.model.1: If number of votes and number of people no match, e mean mistake dey. If you check whether total votes equal 29 students, you fit tell whether one line wrong.
y-m-06-04.s.s3.model.2: If di sum no be 29, one vote miss or dem count am wrong.

y-m-06-06.s.s2.fail.c1: Student numbers must be natural numbers wey be 0 or more.
y-m-06-06.title: If two classes get different winners, combined winner go be one of dem?
y-m-06-06.topic: Combining data: winners for two groups and winner for combined result
y-m-06-06.goal: Realize say plenty examples wey fit no guarantee 'always', and make case where, when dem combine two class tables, one fruit wey no win for either class become winner.
y-m-06-06.material:
Class 1 and Class 2 each get 12 students. Each student choose only apple, tangerine, or pear. Assume each class get only one fruit wey chosen most.
Jihu talk, "If fruit wey most people choose for Class 1 and Class 2 different, fruit wey get most when dem combine both classes go be one of those two."
Jihu check three cases, and statement correct all three times. One case like dis. Class 1: apple 5, tangerine 4, pear 3. Class 2: apple 3, tangerine 5, pear 4. (Together apple 8, tangerine 9, pear 7, so tangerine most.)
y-m-06-06.thinking.0: Checking whether general statement correct even with few fitting examples
y-m-06-06.prereq.0: Comparing size of numbers up to 12
y-m-06-06.prereq.1: Adding numbers for same fruit from tables and reading total
y-m-06-06.s.s1.prompt: Jihu check three cases, and statement correct for all of dem. We fit talk from only dis dat Jihu statement always correct?
y-m-06-06.s.s1.hint.0: Arrange in table which class winner di combined winner be for di three cases.
y-m-06-06.s.s1.hint.1: Write wetin fruit wey no win for either class must look like in each class so e fit become di most when combined.
y-m-06-06.s.s1.o.a: E correct three times, so we fit talk say e always correct.
y-m-06-06.s.s1.r.a: Dis talk about every case just because few examples fit. Other cases still never test.
y-m-06-06.s.s1.o.b: Being correct three times no be evidence at all.
y-m-06-06.s.s1.r.b: Dis see plenty fitting examples as if dem mean nothing. Dem do make you more confident, but dem no settle am.
y-m-06-06.s.s1.o.c: If we check 10 more examples and dem all correct, we fit talk say e always correct.
y-m-06-06.s.s1.r.c: Even if you gather more examples, untested cases still dey. Number of times e correct no fit guarantee 'always'.
y-m-06-06.s.s1.o.d: We no fit know whether e always correct, so look for example where e wrong.
y-m-06-06.s.s1.r.d: Dis thinking separate examples wey dem check from cases wey dem never check.
y-m-06-06.s.s1.o.e: Jihu check am himself, so trust am as e be.
y-m-06-06.s.s1.r.e: Dis thinking say statement correct just because dem check am. E no look at which cases dem check.
y-m-06-06.s.s1.explain: Even if plenty examples fit, e fit go against statement for case wey dem never test. If you find one example wey go against am, 'always' don break. So e good to look for example where e wrong and test am.
y-m-06-06.s.s2.prompt: Make table wey show Jihu statement wrong. Class 1 winner must be apple, Class 2 winner must be tangerine. When dem combine both classes, pear must get more than both apple and tangerine. Each class get 12 students. Enter two different tables. (Class 1: apple a1, tangerine b1, pear c1 / Class 2: apple a2, tangerine b2, pear c2)
y-m-06-06.s.s2.hint.0: First decide how many pear students each class suppose get so pear go be plenty when dem combine.
y-m-06-06.s.s2.hint.1: Split remaining students between apple and tangerine, and check winner condition for each class one by one.
y-m-06-06.s.s2.ok.c1: All na natural numbers 0 or more.
y-m-06-06.s.s2.fail.c2: Class 1 and Class 2 each must add up to 12 students across three fruits.
y-m-06-06.s.s2.ok.c3: For Class 1, apple na di winner.
y-m-06-06.s.s2.fail.c3: For Class 1, apple must get more than both tangerine and pear.
y-m-06-06.s.s2.ok.c4: For Class 2, tangerine na di winner.
y-m-06-06.s.s2.fail.c4: For Class 2, tangerine must get more than apple and pear.
y-m-06-06.s.s2.ok.c5: When dem combine di two classes, pear get more than apple and tangerine. Jihu statement don break.
y-m-06-06.s.s2.fail.c5: When dem combine both classes, pear number must be bigger than apple number and tangerine number. Add each fruit across classes and compare.
y-m-06-06.s.s2.explain: For example, if Class 1 get apple 6, tangerine 1, pear 5, and Class 2 get apple 1, tangerine 6, pear 5, together e be apple 7, tangerine 7, pear 10. Pear no win for either class, but when dem combine am, e be di most. So Jihu statement no always correct.
y-m-06-06.s.s3.prompt: Write why pear, wey no win for either class, fit become di winner when dem combine am.
y-m-06-06.s.s3.hint.0: For di two tables wey you make, write number of pear, apple, and tangerine for each class side by side.
y-m-06-06.s.s3.hint.1: Write di combined numbers, and find how many students di fruit wey win one class get for di other class.
y-m-06-06.s.s3.selfAssess.0: You use numbers from your tables explain di reason?
y-m-06-06.s.s3.selfAssess.1: You talk say "when dem combine" and "inside one class" different?
y-m-06-06.s.s3.model.0: Pear no win for either class, but 5 students for each class choose am, so together na 10 and e become more than apple or tangerine.
y-m-06-06.s.s3.model.1: Apple and tangerine plenty for only one class and small for the other. Pear fairly plenty for both classes, so e be most when dem combine.

y-m-06-07.title: If di way of grouping change, di winner too go change?
y-m-06-07.topic: Sorting: how di most dey change depending on how dem group things
y-m-06-07.goal: Realize say even with di same data, di thing wey be most fit change depending on wetin you group and count as one, and let other people know by saying how you group dem.
y-m-06-07.material:
Each of 26 students for our class choose one game wey dem most want to play during break. 7 choose tag, 6 choose jump rope, 5 choose soccer, 4 choose basketball, and 4 choose dodgeball.
Jihu: "Tag get di most with 7, so tag na di most popular game."
Seoa: "If we group soccer, basketball, and dodgeball as ball games, na 5+4+4=13, so ball games na di most popular."
PE teacher dey wonder which game e good to prepare after seeing dis result.
y-m-06-07.thinking.0: Notice say result dey change depending on grouping rule
y-m-06-07.thinking.1: Make several groupings wey fit conditions
y-m-06-07.thinking.2: Tell listener how you group dem
y-m-06-07.prereq.0: Reading and comparing numbers from table
y-m-06-07.prereq.1: Reading size of several numbers put together
y-m-06-07.s.s1.prompt: How we fit understand wetin Jihu and Seoa talk? Choose di one wey fit best.
y-m-06-07.s.s1.hint.0: Point in table to cells wey get di numbers each person use.
y-m-06-07.s.s1.hint.1: Put side by side di biggest number when dem count same data "one game at a time" and when dem count "grouped by kind".
y-m-06-07.s.s1.o.a: Na only Seoa correct. If we decide to count games grouped by kind, na so e be.
y-m-06-07.s.s1.r.a: Dis see counting each game separately as wrong from beginning. Wetin count as one thing depend on your choice, and if you state your choice, you fit explain dis thinking too.
y-m-06-07.s.s1.o.b: One of dem calculate one number wrong.
y-m-06-07.s.s1.r.b: 5+4+4 na 13, and 7 na one number for table. You fit check both people numbers for table.
y-m-06-07.s.s1.o.c: Dem both fit check for table, and winner dey change depending on how you group and count.
y-m-06-07.s.s1.r.c: Dis notice say when way of counting change with same data, statement too dey change.
y-m-06-07.s.s1.o.d: Data no plenty enough to talk either way.
y-m-06-07.s.s1.r.d: From table alone, you fit check both people numbers. Wetin no settle na deciding "wetin dem count as one thing".
y-m-06-07.s.s1.o.e: Na only Jihu correct. If we decide to count each game separately, na so e be.
y-m-06-07.s.s1.r.e: Dis see grouping and counting method as wrong from beginning. If you state your choice, you fit explain dis thinking too.
y-m-06-07.s.s1.explain: You fit check Jihu 7 and Seoa 13 with numbers for table. If you count each game separately, tag na the most; if you group as ball games, ball games na the most. Any way, if you talk "how you count", you fit explain both statements.
y-m-06-07.s.s1.acc.0: If we decide to count games grouped by kind, wetin Seoa talk correct. But we gatz say na so we decide to count.
y-m-06-07.s.s1.acc.1: If we decide to count each game separately, wetin Jihu talk correct. But we gatz say na so we decide to count.
y-m-06-07.s.s2.prompt: Gym fit hold maximum 10 students in one place. Teacher wan group exactly two of soccer, basketball, dodgeball, and jump rope into one team, so number of students for team go be above tag (7 students) and no more than 10. Write 1 if you choose am and 0 if not, and make two different groupings. (Student numbers: soccer 5, basketball 4, dodgeball 4, jump rope 6)
y-m-06-07.s.s2.hint.0: Choose two, write student number, and check whether e bigger than 7 and no more than 10.
y-m-06-07.s.s2.hint.1: Test wetin happen if you group game with most students together with game with fewest.
y-m-06-07.s.s2.fail.c1: Write only 1 if you choose am and 0 if you no choose am.
y-m-06-07.s.s2.ok.c3: Student number bigger than 7 and no more than 10.
y-m-06-07.s.s2.fail.c3: Add student numbers for games wey you choose and check whether e bigger than 7 and no more than 10.
y-m-06-07.s.s2.explain: Groupings wey fit conditions na soccer+basketball (9 students), soccer+dodgeball (9 students), basketball+dodgeball (8 students), basketball+jump rope (10 students), and dodgeball+jump rope (10 students), five altogether. Soccer+jump rope na 11 students, so e no work. Number of students for team dey change depending which two you group.
y-m-06-07.s.s3.prompt: You wan tell PE teacher which game e good to prepare. Talk how you group and count to get result, and write am in two or three sentences.
y-m-06-07.s.s3.hint.0: Write di first sentence first, so teacher fit see "wetin dem count as one thing" by reading only one line.
y-m-06-07.s.s3.hint.1: Write di biggest number wey come from each of di two counting methods.
y-m-06-07.s.s3.placeholder: Example: Teacher, if we count games ..., ...
y-m-06-07.s.s3.selfAssess.0: Teacher fit tell how dem count result only by reading wetin I write?
y-m-06-07.s.s3.selfAssess.1: You show results of both counting methods, or if you show only one, you talk so?
y-m-06-07.s.s3.model.0: Teacher, if we count each game separately, tag get di most with 7 students. But if we group soccer, basketball, and dodgeball as ball games and count, na 13 students, so ball games na the most. Abeg keep dis in mind when you prepare balls.
y-m-06-07.s.s3.model.1: If we group and count ball games, soccer 5, basketball 4, and dodgeball 4 add up to 13 students, wey be di most. But if we count each game name separately, tag with 7 students na winner. E depend on how we count.

y-m-06-08.title: Comparing picture graphs for three classes
y-m-06-08.topic: Picture graphs: when number each picture represent different from graph to graph
y-m-06-08.goal: Learn say number wey one picture represent fit different from graph to graph, confirm say you no fit judge more or fewer from number of pictures alone, make example where number of pictures and number of books no match, and state agreements wey make graph easy to read.
y-m-06-08.material:
Books wey three classes read for school library in April show for picture graph for each class. Number of books one picture (◎) represent different for each graph. For Class 1 and Class 3, one ◎ na 10 books, and for Class 2, one ◎ na 5 books.
Class 1: 4 ◎
Class 2: 7 ◎
Class 3: 5 ◎
Seoyun talk, 'Class wey get most pictures read most books.'
y-m-06-08.thinking.0: Finding line in solution wey jump ahead without reason
y-m-06-08.thinking.1: Making example where number of pictures and books no match
y-m-06-08.thinking.2: Comparing agreements wey make graph easy to read
y-m-06-08.prereq.0: Reading picture graph where one picture represent 10
y-m-06-08.s.s1.prompt: Follow Seoyun thinking line by line and choose one line wey hard to trust.
y-m-06-08.s.s1.hint.0: For each class, write number of pictures side by side with number of books one picture represent.
y-m-06-08.s.s1.hint.1: Calculate and write number of books for each class, then compare with number of pictures.
y-m-06-08.s.s1.line.3: Class wey get most pictures na Class 2, so Class 2 na class wey read most books.
y-m-06-08.s.s1.explain: Line 4 wrong. Counting pictures for lines 1 to 3 correct, but for Class 2 graph one picture na 5 books, so number of pictures no tell number of books. Class 1 get 40 books, Class 2 get 35, and Class 3 get 50, so Class 3 get di most.
y-m-06-08.s.s2.prompt: Make two different cases where Class A get more pictures than Class B but fewer books. For each class, enter number of pictures (◎) (1 to 9) and number of books one picture represent (1 to 20).
y-m-06-08.s.s2.hint.0: First decide how many books one picture represent for each class, then change number of pictures and calculate number of books.
y-m-06-08.s.s2.hint.1: Write number of pictures and number of books for each class separately, then compare both cases.
y-m-06-08.s.s2.var.a: Number of pictures for Class A
y-m-06-08.s.s2.var.p: Number of books one picture represent for Class A
y-m-06-08.s.s2.var.b: Number of pictures for Class B
y-m-06-08.s.s2.var.q: Number of books one picture represent for Class B
y-m-06-08.s.s2.ok.c1: Number of pictures na natural number from 1 to 9, and number of books na natural number from 1 to 20.
y-m-06-08.s.s2.fail.c1: Abeg use natural number from 1 to 9 for number of pictures, and natural number from 1 to 20 for number of books one picture represent.
y-m-06-08.s.s2.fail.c2: Class A must get more pictures than Class B.
y-m-06-08.s.s2.fail.c3: Number of books for Class A (number of pictures x books per picture) must be less than Class B.
y-m-06-08.s.s2.explain: For example, if Class A get 7 ◎ (5 books each, 35 books) and Class B get 4 ◎ (10 books each, 40 books), Class A get more pictures but fewer books. When number each picture represent different, you no fit tell which class get more books just from number of pictures.
y-m-06-08.s.s3.prompt: Choose all graph rules wey make people reading graphs from several classes no confuse.
y-m-06-08.s.s3.hint.0: Imagine friend seeing one graph wey dem draw with each rule for first time, then reading am.
y-m-06-08.s.s3.hint.1: For each rule, check one by one whether friend fit find number of books.
y-m-06-08.s.s3.o.a: Each graph decide by itself how many books one picture represent and no write am down
y-m-06-08.s.s3.r.a: If value different from graph to graph and dem no write am down, reader fit compare wrongly by looking only at number of pictures.
y-m-06-08.s.s3.o.b: Write for each graph how many books one picture represent.
y-m-06-08.s.s3.r.b: If dem write value, reader fit calculate number of books. Rule wey make graphs wey dem dey compare use same value make dem easier to read too.
y-m-06-08.s.s3.o.c: Agree in advance say side with more pictures also get more books
y-m-06-08.s.s3.r.c: Dis decide winner by number of pictures, no be number of books. E fit no match actual number of books.
y-m-06-08.s.s3.o.d: Make graphs wey dem go compare use same number for wetin one picture represent.
y-m-06-08.s.s3.r.d: If one picture get same value, you fit compare by only counting pictures. You still need rule to write di value too.
y-m-06-08.s.s3.explain: To compare directly by number of pictures, graphs wey dem dey compare must use same number for wetin one picture represent. If values different, you gatz write for each graph how many books one picture represent so readers no confuse.
